Challah

Served at: Rosh Hashanah (Jewish New Year)

Serves 8-10Prep 30 minCook 30 min

Challah is a traditional braided bread enjoyed during Jewish holidays, especially Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year. On this festive occasion, the bread is often made round to symbolize the cycle of the year and continuity of life, making it a meaningful centerpiece for the holiday meal.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (480 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (1 packet) active dry yeast
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup (240 ml) warm water (about 110°F/43°C)
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) vegetable oil
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 egg (for egg wash)
  • 1 tablespoon poppy seeds or sesame seeds (optional)

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve yeast and 1 tablespoon sugar in warm water; let stand for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, remaining sugar, and salt.
  3. In a separate bowl, beat 2 eggs with oil and vanilla extract.
  4. Add the yeast mixture and egg mixture to the dry ingredients and stir until a dough forms.
  5. Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  6. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  7. Punch down the dough and divide it into three equal pieces.
  8. Roll each piece into a long rope, then braid the ropes together, pinching the ends to seal and shaping into a circle for Rosh Hashanah.
  9. Place the braided dough on a parchment-lined baking sheet, cover, and let rise for another 30-45 minutes.
  10. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  11. Beat the remaining egg and brush it over the loaf for a shiny crust.
  12. Sprinkle with poppy or sesame seeds if desired.
  13. Bake for 25-30 minutes, until the challah is golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped.
  14. Let cool on a wire rack before serving.

Tips

  • For a sweeter challah, add 1/4 cup honey to the dough.
  • Use bread flour instead of all-purpose flour for a chewier texture.
  • To make individual rolls, divide dough into smaller pieces and braid or shape as desired.
